findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed a container of open milk and corn salsa to be held past date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking practices. Milk and corn were both discarded, ensure any TCS item is discarded after its 7 day date marking maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.

(B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw fish to be stored next to raw chicken in kitchen line prep cooler. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper storage order, fish was moved to a location above chicken. Ensure facility is following proper storage order to prevent any possible cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(D) Temperature Measuring Devices. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Observed the following items to be stored on the floor:
1) A bag of flour was observed to be resting on the floor in the prep/dish machine room. 
2) A container holding beef was observed to be resting on the floor in back walk in cooler. 
3) A container holding s’mores supplies was observed to be resting on the floor in bar. 

Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper location for storing foods. All items were relocated to at least 6 inches off of ground. Ensure any food item is kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed no allergen training to have been completed by any CFM’s available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, allergen training will be completed. Ensure all CFM’s have completed the required allergen training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed multiple employees to wash hands incorrectly. Hands were washed with soap and warm water, but no barrier was used to turn off the faucet handles. Discussed with all employees who washed hands incorrectly. Ensure a paper towel is used to turn off the faucet handles in order to prevent cross contamination of hands. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following non-food contact surfaces in need of cleaning:
1. Food splash along the walls near the hot holding station/expo window to server area.
2. The kitchen 3 compartment sink spray squeezer handle has a significant amount of food debris/mold.
3. Walk-in cooler fans in the kitchen and back walk-in cooler (near bathrooms) have a layer of dust.
4. Top of the dish machine in the prep area with the 3 compartment sink has a layer of food debris/dirt.

#1 and 3 are repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/7/23. Discussed with employees and PIC. Clean before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy for the facility. PIC indicated it must have gotten lost. Provided new copy of the policy SCDPH utilizes. Facility has bleach to perform procedure. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed ice dumped in the kitchen hand sink at the beginning of the inspection. Ensure hand sinks are for hand washing only. Do not use the hand sink as a dump sink. Cease practice. Ensure staff is aware. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the ice machine in the prep/dish machine area to have a layer of mold on the interior baffle. Inspector asked PIC to remove all the ice and wash, rinse, sanitize the interior of the machine including the baffle. PIC cleaned during the inspection. Ensure routine cleaning of food-contact surfaces. Ice is considered a food. Ensure staff is aware to frequently clean the interior of the ice machine. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed multiple bottom reach-in prep coolers to lack thermometers. Mini fridge in the server area did not have a thermometer as well. Ensure all cold holding units have thermometers. Discussed with PIC. Ensure extra thermometers are available at the facility in order to replace as needed. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed the bar staff to be utilizing spray bottles of quaternary ammonium based sanitizer for cleaning. Rags were being used with the spray bottle. Cease practice. Ensure spray bottles of sanitizer are utilized with paper towels and disposed. In-use rags should be kept within sanitizer buckets when not being utilized. Ensure appropriate concentration of sanitizer (200-400 ppm of quat) in the bucket. Either method will suffice, but keep it consistent. Discussed with PIC. Correct the process with staff.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Observed no quaternary ammonium test strips for the facility. Provided samples. PIC/main cook indicated the facility had just run out. Ensure extra test strips are available for both types of sanitizer being used at the facility (quat for spray bottles and sani buckets; bleach for dish machines). Bleach test strips were available to accurately test the dish machine concentrations of sanitizer. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. Food splash along the walls near the hot holding station/expo window to server area. 
2. Food debris on the seal area and base of the reach-in hot holding unit.
3. The fryers need pulled away from the cook line -> significant debris under the fryers. Clean the area.
4. Several walk-in cooler fans needed cleaned of dust: kitchen, beer cooler across from server station, and back beer cooler.
5. Hard water was noted within the main kitchen dish machine. De-lime the dish machine and use a stainless steel scrubber if needed to remove the hard water within the interior of the dish machine.
6. Dust was noted on most of the vent system and ceiling within the prep/dish machine area.
7. Sweeping behind shelving within the kitchen walk-in cooler.

Ensure routine cleaning of Non-food contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC. Clean the above mentioned areas.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Both men and women’s hand sinks (4x) need re-caulked to the wall. Sinks are coming away from the wall.
2. The roof appears to be leaking and creating water damage within the facility. Main prep/dish area of the kitchen has significant water damage on the ceiling, as well as the storage area in the back with 1 reach-in freezer and alcohol storage. PIC indicated a new roof will be put on the building at some point in the future; however, the ceilings of the kitchen and dry storage need addressed after this occurs. Ceilings should be smooth and easily cleanable.

Discussed with PIC. Correct #1 before next routine inspection. #2 will be monitored with facility. Food Program Manager, Colleen Kelley, was contacted with photos to address the roof/ceiling damage. CK will contact facility owner to discuss.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed a large amount of food handler’s licenses to be expired. Ensure employees re-do food handler’s licenses and keep valid. License is valid for 3 years. Discussed with PIC. Ensure new hires complete food handler’s certification within 30 days of employment. Ensure public health folder is updated with valid licenses by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed multiple allergen training certifications to be expired. Certification is valid for 3 years. All certified food protection manager’s must have a valid allergen training certification license. Discussed with PIC. Provided educational hand out to re-take course. Complete by next routine inspection and update public health folder with copies of valid licenses.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet. Correct hand washing procedures were discussed and the PIC is instructed to ensure that correct hand washing procedures are followed.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). 

A gallon of milk in the bar cooler is observed partial empty and without a date mark. Education took place and a date was given of the earliest possible date to correct.
